title: real american
description: This piece is dedicated to immigrants—too often rendered invisible in the American narrative. The green card, while symbolizing legal residency, still carries the label "resident alien," a term that strips individuals of humanity and reinforces the idea they will never be seen as truly American.

title: computers.json
description: What if we made a home for our computers? This is not an archive of the product itself, but an intimate story about the person who owns the computer. Data isn’t always shown in numbers or strings; it can be shown by how many stickers you have. Even the dents, scratches, and worn-down keys are data about how you treat your technology. These intimate details invite others to see the imperfections and personalizations. Computers.json is the home for our computers, and I want YOU to be a part of it!

title: ceo wAIfus
description: wAifu CEOs is a critique of humans’ relationships with autonomous machines that have no consciousness. When did algorithms and probability become a replacement for human intimacy? In this “AI era,” people are forming romantic relationships with their AI agents or even using them as therapists. This interactive body pillow is a satirical piece: users can sleep with their AI agent or talk to it like a human (and it talks back!). Instead of displaying characterized versions of AI agents, I put the people at the forefront of these AI companies, the CEOs, front and center. Yes, this is the Sam Altman body pillow.

title: rip computer angel
description: what if a computer didn’t only store your digital data, but also the physical data you carry with you all the time? this is e-waste turned into a fashion wearable–a piece where you hold your physical items instead of pictures or documents in a folder. what was once part of a system becomes memorabilia of what it used to be, upcycled into a new artifact. it’s a non-functioning computer, where the user has to process all the instructions themselves. it’s still a machine, just one that holds a different kind of data.

title: dreamscape
description: Dreamscape is a fashion collection for the freaks, the weirdos, the “too much-ers,” whimsical wizards & late-diagnosed neurodivergent gals. This is a love letter to growing up as a neurodivergent girl, told through the language of lolita fashion—a J-fashion subculture defined by anti-consumerism, feminism, and radical self-expression.

title: reminiscence
description: This work revolves around memory—specifically how our memories evolve over time, particularly with sentimental items we've lost over the years. In these interviews, I ask my friends to recall a childhood plushie and describe it from memory. I recreate the plushie based on their descriptions and recollection. Each plushie was handmade, serving as an extension of my love for these friends. Our material objects are an extension of ourselves. Sometimes the material object is all that we have left. And it the only thing that we can attach as humans. Memory becomes intertwined with the object itself

title: connections of love
description: Exploring different connections of love through a queer lens
